title: Emergencies & Health
description: Low probability, high cost. These are worth over-learning precisely because you'd be using them under stress.

phrases.registerNotes: Unambiguous, and understood instantly. 助けて alone is fine in a genuine emergency — politeness stops mattering.
薬局 (やっきょく) is a pharmacy, for anything less urgent.
phrases.audioHint: びょういんはどこですか

phrases.registerNotes: General-purpose 'something is wrong with me'. Follow by pointing at where it hurts.

phrases.japanese: 救急車を呼んでください
phrases.registerNotes: Emergency numbers: 119 for ambulance and fire, 110 for police. Ambulances are free to call in Japan.
phrases.audioHint: きゅうきゅうしゃをよんでください

phrases.japanese: 警察を呼んでください
phrases.registerNotes: 110 for police. 交番 (こうばん) is the neighbourhood police box — there's one near most stations.
phrases.audioHint: けいさつをよんでください

phrases.registerNotes: Point as you say it. Solves the entire vocabulary problem of body parts in one phrase.
At a 薬局 (pharmacy) or ドラッグストア. Painkillers and cold medicine are over the counter.
Report it at a 交番. Japan's lost-property rate is genuinely remarkable — it is often worth reporting.
phrases.audioHint: さいふをなくしました

phrases.japanese: 英語を話せる人はいますか
phrases.romaji: eigo o hanaseru hito wa imasu ka
phrases.english: Is there anyone who speaks English?
phrases.registerNotes: Better than asking one person directly in a hospital or police station — it escalates to whoever can actually help.
phrases.audioHint: えいごをはなせるひとはいますか

phrases.japanese: アレルギーがあります。これを見てください

furigana.b: アレルギーがあります。これを

phrases.romaji: arerugī ga arimasu. kore o mite kudasai
phrases.english: I have an allergy. Please look at this.
phrases.registerNotes: Pair with an allergy card written in Japanese on your phone. In a medical emergency this is the sentence that matters.
phrases.audioHint: アレルギーがあります。これをみてください
